english_classification.chapter_note: Overwhelmingly substrate chapter. The teaching describes three conduits (lihme) connecting heavenly powers to earthly domains, through which life ascends and waste descends. The entire cosmological architecture—conduits, roots, the wheel of stars, the Ambassador myth, cosmic geography—maps domain to domain without ever reaching into the contemporary world. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation vocabulary detected at all. The only later material consists of thin dialogue frame formulas wrapping the teaching. The Persian dialogue tradition is strong here: the disciples' questions about zodiacal authority and conduit hierarchy reveal teaching structure. Heavy lacunae in the later paragraphs (22-24) but the surviving words are consistently cosmological.
